AfterDeath.issue: THE HOOK IS THE WRONG ONE, and the consequences are observable. C# lets the death HAPPEN: Hook.ShouldDie returns true, CreatureCmd.cs:507-508 fires InvokeDiedEvent and computes shouldRemoveFromCombat = false (from this power's ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath), then AfterDeath sets isReviving and calls TestSubject.TriggerDeadState() -- leaving the Test Subject **dead at 0 HP, retained in combat**, with the combat held open by ShouldStopCombatFromEnding. The sim instead PREVENTS the death from `should_die` (powers.py:3365-3370 returns False), and cmds.py:106-113 then floors the creature at **1 HP** and leaves `is_dead` False. Three observable consequences. (1) HP: 1 vs 0, which conformance asserts on directly. (2) damage_pipeline gap G4 -- C# locks the AfterDamageReceived-skip decision to the pre-Kill snapshot so an arithmetically lethal hit permanently skips the victim's on-damage-received powers, while the sim resets HP to 1 first and only then tests `target.is_dead` (cmds.py:121), so the Test Subject's Enrage and every other on_damage_received listener fires in the sim and not in the game. Not re-verdicted (rule 3). (3) Feed: `Feed.cs:38` computes `shouldTriggerFatal = cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` and AdaptablePower does NOT override it (default true), and `WasTargetKilled` is true even when the death is prevented (DamageResult.cs:89-99 says so in as many words: "This will return true even if the creature was resurrected afterwards (Fairy in a Bottle, etc.)", with :97 giving exactly that example), so **the game grants the +3 max HP for Feeding the Test Subject to death**; the sim's `if target.is_dead` (cards/feed.py:45) is False, so it grants nothing -- and the sim's own docstring (cards/feed.py:17-18) asserts the opposite behaviour is correct. EXECUTED (sim side): after a lethal Strike the Test Subject sits at hp 1 with `is_dead` False. LIVE: Feed is a ported Rare Ironclad Attack and the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss. Third-file citations, not hashed here. **THE SHARED OBSERVABLE, WITH A PORTED WITNESS -- Hook.AfterDeath fires on BOTH C# branches and in the sim on NEITHER.** CreatureCmd.cs:519 dispatches `Hook.AfterDeath(..., wasRemovalPrevented: false, deathAnimLength)` on the real-death branch and CreatureCmd.cs:566 dispatches `Hook.AfterDeath(..., wasRemovalPrevented: true, 0f)` on the prevention branch, in both cases to EVERY hook listener and not just to the dying creature's own powers. The sim fires `hooks.on_death` only on its real-death arm (cmds.py:105); its prevention arm (cmds.py:106-113) fires nothing but `after_preventing_death`. So a death any of these three powers touches reaches NO on_death listener at all. WITNESS: `GremlinHorn.cs:24-32` overrides AfterDeath with **no** `wasRemovalPrevented` guard -- its only test is `target.Side != base.Owner.Creature.Side` -- so the game grants +1 Energy (PlayerCmd.GainEnergy, :29) and DRAWS 1 CARD (CardPileCmd.Draw, :30) every time the Test Subject, the Waterfall Giant, Fogmog's Eye with Teeth or The Obscura's Parafright dies, prevented or not, while `sts2_rl/relics/gremlin_horn.py:18-22` (`def on_death`) never runs on any of them. LIVE: Gremlin Horn is a ported Uncommon relic and all four appliers are ported enemies (monsters/glory/test_subject.py, monsters/underdocks/waterfall_giant.py:148-151 + rooms.py:139, monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py:34-35, monsters/hive/the_obscura.py:38-39). The extra draw is not cosmetic: it perturbs the draw/discard piles for the rest of the fight and, under conformance replay, the RNG stream for the rest of the run. ONE MECHANISM, ONE VERDICT (binding rule 3): power/adaptable, power/illusion and power/steam_eruption all implement a C# AfterDeath body by returning False from `should_die` (powers.py:3365-3369, :1566-1570, :2016-2020), so all three run the sim's single death-PREVENTION branch (cmds.py:106-113) where C# runs the REAL-DEATH branch (CreatureCmd.cs:505-559). None of the three overrides ShouldDie, and all three bodies sit behind `!wasRemovalPrevented` (AdaptablePower.cs:34, IllusionPower.cs:79, SteamEruptionPower.cs:17) -- i.e. they are explicitly EXCLUDED from the branch the sim is executing. All three therefore carry `gap`; steam_eruption's `deliberate-divergence` was corrected to `gap` in the 2026-07-26 review fix pass. The canonical statement of the shared observable (the Gremlin Horn witness) is on power/adaptable's AfterDeath entry.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: LIVE, and it upgrades a seam gap that was recorded as un-demonstrated. C#'s PowerCmd.Apply<T> refuses to apply anything to a creature `CanReceivePowers` says no to, and CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting -- which is exactly what this override's own doc comment says it is for ("This is so the ... doesn't receive POWERS while it is reviving"). The sim wires should_allow_hitting into DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:51-52) but NOT into PowerCmd.apply, which has no such guard at all. That is `power_cmd` gap **G6**, whose text says "No concrete broken interaction is demonstrated (spot-checked callers apply powers only to already-resolved targets)". **That is now falsified. EXECUTED:** a TEST_SUBJECT_BOSS combat (the Test Subject starts with powers ['adaptable', 'enrage']), a lethal Strike, then Vulnerable 2 from the player -- the sim reports `is_reviving True`, `should_allow_hitting(ts) False`, and then still lands `Vulnerable(2)` on the reviving boss, where the game refuses the application outright. Control: a 10-damage Strike in the same window returns 0 HP lost, proving the predicate IS wired into the damage path and only the power path is missing it. Rule-6 co-occurrence: the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss and applies this power to itself at combat start, Bash/Vulnerable is ported basic-pool Ironclad content, and the revive window is the remainder of the player's turn after the killing blow -- the ordinary flow of the fight, not a contrived state. The same override exists on IllusionPower and ReattachPower, so all three carry it. Verdict carried per rule 3; the seam record is not edited (half B does not own audit/records/seam/** or docs/audit/seams/**) -- reported in .superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 2.3. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldStopCombatFromEnding.issue: No sim counterpart. C# reads this through Hook.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding at CombatManager.cs:196, i.e. inside the win check: while ANY power on ANY creature returns true the combat cannot end. The sim has no such hook -- `hooks.py` defines no `should_stop_combat_from_ending` -- and `combat.py:272-277` decides the win purely from `is_gone` over the non-minion enemies. The sim reaches the same OUTCOME by a different route in each case (see this record's death entry), but the mechanism is absent, so a future power that wants to hold combat open without also preventing a death or adding a creature has nothing to hook. Dormant: all five ported overrides (AdaptablePower, InfestedPower, SteamEruptionPower, StockPower, SurprisePower) are paired with either a death prevention or a mid-death spawn that keeps `_all_enemies_dead()` false on its own. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL HOME (added 2026-07-26): this mechanism now also carries `gap` at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8c, which owns the missing hook surface itself; same verdict at every site per rule 3.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. The sim never removes powers on death at all -- a grep of cmds.py's kill/death path finds no `powers.clear()` or per-power removal, and cmds.py:96-105 goes straight from the HP write to should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death -- so `false` is the sim's universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. Faithful HERE. The inverse is a real machinery gap owned by nobody: the C# DEFAULT is `true`, so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is. That is reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3 rather than verdicted on this unit, because it is an engine-wide absence and not this power's divergence. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: Part of the should_die-for-AfterDeath mechanism, carried as its own entry because it survives any fix that only re-slots the AfterDeath body. cmds.py:112 writes `target.hp = 1` and stops. C# does NOT heal the creature: CreatureCmd.cs:560-571 leaves it at 0 HP, fires Hook.AfterDeath(wasRemovalPrevented: true) and Hook.AfterPreventingDeath, and then, `if (creature.IsDead)`, RE-ENTERS `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` -- up to 10 times before throwing InvalidOperationException (:562-565). So in the game a preventer must actually raise the creature's HP (Fairy in a Bottle heals; these three do not, which is why they take C#'s DEATH branch and not this one), whereas the sim's single silent `hp = 1` makes any prevention permanent and models neither the re-entry nor the 10-deep bail-out. Two consequences beyond the 1-vs-0 HP that conformance asserts on directly: the sim cannot express a prevention that fails, and the sim's own steam_eruption HP restore only runs because this floor makes `target.is_dead` False at cmds.py:121 (damage_pipeline gap G4). Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.

guards.what: The non-damage kill path: CreatureCmd.kill reproduces both arms but fires no on_damage_received
guards.issue: Part of the same mechanism, at the second of the sim's two death sites. `CreatureCmd.kill` (cmds.py:191-205) mirrors DamageCmd.deal's should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death fork and the same `target.hp = 1` prevention floor, but it is not a damage event, so it fires neither on_damage_received nor after_preventing_death. Consequences: (a) power/steam_eruption's HP restore (powers.py:2022-2033) lives on on_damage_received and therefore does not run here at all, leaving the Waterfall Giant at hp 1 instead of the 999999999 WaterfallGiant.cs:305 sets; (b) the preventer never learns the death was prevented. DORMANT for these three powers today -- the only ported non-damage kill of a steam_eruption owner is the giant's own `_explode` (monsters/underdocks/waterfall_giant.py:142-145), which runs AFTER `_about_to_blow` removed the power at :140, and nothing kills the Test Subject or an Illusion off the damage path. Named trigger: any ported non-damage kill reaching a creature that still holds one of these three powers -- SandpitPower._expire (powers.py:2610-2619) and TheGambitPower (powers.py:3816-3829) are the two ported callers of CreatureCmd.kill outside a monster's own move. Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.
